description: Field-level encryption for Entity Framework Core. AES-GCM authenticated encryption, key rotation, blind-index equality lookups, exact Contains/StartsWith/EndsWith search and in-application sorting on encrypted columns, a query guard that throws instead of returning wrong results, verified batch re-encryption (CBC to GCM, key rotation), convention-based AutoEncryption, ML PII classifier, Crypto Sentinel decryption-anomaly monitoring, email/webhook alerting and DPDP/GDPR compliance reports. Core encryption, key rotation, blind-index and search run without a license key; a license key unlocks the ML PII classifier, Crypto Sentinel, email/webhook alerting and DPDP/GDPR-ready compliance reporting.
releaseNotes:
Version 10.4.0

			WHAT CHANGED SINCE 10.3.0
			- New: tolerant decryption (opt-in). With UseEncryption(provider, new EncryptionOptions { OnDecryptionFailure = DecryptionFailurePolicy.ReturnNull }), a string, byte[], dictionary or JSON column whose stored value cannot be decrypted is read as null, logged, and no longer fails the whole query. The default is unchanged: an unreadable value still throws. AutoEncryptionOptions.Encryption applies the same setting to UseAutoEncryption.
			- Tested on real databases (PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.4, SQL Server 2022) with EF Core 8, 9 and 10. Before, the real-database tests ran on EF Core 10 only. No library change was needed.
			- There are no other code changes: licensing behavior, dependencies and the stored data format are the same as 10.3.0.

			CHANGED IN 10.3.0
			- Licensing validation is back (10.2.0 had it switched off, so it granted every feature with no key). On a local development machine nothing is checked or logged and every feature works with no key. A deployment with no valid key fails at startup. See LICENSE BEHAVIOR below.

			ALSO CHANGED IN 10.2.0 (its notes repeated the 10.1.0 notes and did not list these)
			- New WhereBlindIn method for IN-list lookups on a blind-indexed column.
			- Stricter query guard: with UseEncryptedQueryGuard, equality (==, !=) and IN-list lookups (list.Contains) on a randomized (AES-GCM) encrypted column throw EncryptedQueryNotSupportedException, because they silently matched no rows. Null checks, and equality on a deterministic provider such as the legacy fixed-IV AesCryptoProvider, are still allowed.
			- EncryptedQueryNotSupportedException constructor gained an optional fourth parameter, hint. Code that only catches the exception is unaffected. Code that constructs it must be recompiled.
			- Fixed: MigrationCryptoProvider could fail to read about 1 in 256 legacy AES-CBC values whose first bytes looked like a GCM envelope with an unregistered key ID. It now tries the legacy decryptor first, and still reports a genuinely missing key.
			- Dependencies updated (see DEPENDENCIES).

			BREAKING CHANGES
			- Since 10.2.0 (changed in 10.3.0): licensing enforcement returns. An app that calls AddDataEncryptionML without a valid key fails at startup in production-like environments, as it did before 10.2.0.
			- Since 10.1.0: LicenseEnforcer.Enforce returns a new value, Outcome.AllowedInDevelopment, for an unlicensed local development machine under Auto mode (it used to return AllowedWithWarning). Code that switched on that result needs a new case.
			- Since 10.1.0: the guard change and the exception constructor change above. The net10.0 package requires Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore 10.0.14 or later.
			- Nothing in 10.4.0 itself breaks existing code: the existing UseEncryption(provider) overload is unchanged, and the default failure policy is still to throw.

			NEW AND REMOVED APIS
			- 10.4.0 added: DecryptionFailurePolicy, DecryptionFailure, EncryptionOptions, the UseEncryption(ModelBuilder, IEncryptionCryptoProvider, EncryptionOptions) overload, and AutoEncryptionOptions.Encryption. Removed: none.
			- Added in 10.3.0: LicenseEnforcer.Outcome.AllowedInDevelopment, LicenseGate.IsDevelopmentMode, and an optional developmentMode parameter on the LicenseGate constructor.
			- Added in 10.2.0: WhereBlindIn and the optional hint parameter on EncryptedQueryNotSupportedException.
			- Also present since 10.1.0: HasSearchIndex, AsEncrypted (WhereContains, WhereStartsWith, WhereEndsWith, OrderBy, ThenBy), EncryptedSortOptions, SearchIndexBackfill, UseEncryptedQueryGuard, WithNormalization and NormalizeForQuery, EncryptionRotator with RotationOptions and checkpoint stores.

			DEPENDENCIES (unchanged in 10.4.0)
			- Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore and Microsoft.Extensions.* (net10.0): 10.0.14. The net8.0 and net9.0 builds use the newest 8.0.* and 9.0.* patch releases.
			- MailKit 4.18.2. Microsoft.ML and Microsoft.ML.TimeSeries 5.0.1.
			- Security: MailKit 4.18.2 brings in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs 10.0.13, which fixes advisories GHSA-846f-f764-76mx (high severity) and GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7 (moderate) that affected the Pkcs version used by 10.1.0 and earlier.

			STORED DATA FORMAT
			- Unchanged. Values written by earlier versions, AES-GCM or legacy AES-CBC, read exactly as before. Nothing needs re-encrypting to upgrade.
			- HasSearchIndex adds an optional nullable column named after the property plus SearchIndex. It needs a database migration and a one-time SearchIndexBackfill for existing rows. WhereBlindIn uses the existing blind-index column and needs no schema change.

			LICENSE BEHAVIOR
			- The license is checked only when AddDataEncryptionML is called. UseEncryption, blind index, search, sorting, tolerant decryption and EncryptionRotator never check it.
			- Community needs no key: field encryption, key rotation, cloud KMS, blind indexing, search and auto-encryption. Enterprise needs a key: ML classifier, Crypto Sentinel, email and webhook alerts, custom alert channels, decryption audit trail, compliance reports.
			- Local development (default mode Auto): everything works with or without a key, every feature is available, and no license warning or error is shown.
			- Deployed (Auto): without a valid key it throws LicenseValidationException at startup in Kubernetes, managed cloud, a container (unless the environment is Development), or when the environment is Production or Staging.
			- To log a warning instead of failing, set Enforcement.Mode to WarnOnly in the options, or set the environment variable EFCRYPTOML_LICENSE_ENFORCEMENT to WarnOnly. Paid features then stay off until a key is added. Strict mode fails everywhere, including a developer machine.
			- Plans: Community (free, under $2,000 annual revenue), Enterprise Annual ($2,999/yr), Enterprise 3-Year ($5,999 prepaid), Enterprise 5-Year ($6,999 prepaid), all Enterprise plans with unlimited developers and projects. See https://efcore-encryption.com/#plans

			KNOWN LIMITS
			- Tolerant decryption applies to reference-type columns only (string, byte[], dictionaries, JSON classes). Numeric columns (long, decimal, double, nullable or not) always throw, because a null cannot be returned for them and a default of 0 would silently be wrong.
			- With tolerant decryption on, treat an entity that holds an unreadable (null) value as read-only for that property: saving a change to it would overwrite the original ciphertext. EncryptionRotator refuses to run over a tolerant column for the same reason.
			- Tolerant failures are always passed to OnFailure, but the log is throttled to one warning per property every 10 seconds, with a count of the failures since. The log and the report carry no row identifier, ciphertext, plaintext or exception message.
			- Sorting an encrypted column runs in the application and needs a maxRows cap. If more rows match, it throws and never truncates.
			- Contains search needs a term of at least 3 characters. StartsWith and EndsWith accept shorter terms.
			- The search index reveals which rows share short fragments of text, not the text itself. Use a dedicated blind-index key. It has not had an independent security review.
			- Existing rows are not searchable until SearchIndexBackfill has run. On PostgreSQL a trigram GIN index on the search column is recommended; the published timings were measured without one.
			- EncryptionRotator needs a single-column primary key and a concurrency token (or AllowWithoutConcurrencyToken), and stops on a row that cannot be decrypted.
			- Unicode normalization of search terms is not performed. Not tested: concurrent load, tables over 300,000 rows, MariaDB, managed cloud databases.

			Roadmap: https://github.com/efcore-encryption/EntityFrameworkCore.Crypto.DataEncryption/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
